node.label: Jack P Greene
node.date_label: Peripheries and Center (1986) · Pursuits of Happiness (1988) · Atlantic History: A Critical Appraisal: co-edited with Philip D. Morgan (2008)
node.description: A historian of colonial British America and comparative Atlantic history. In his 2019 conversation with Miguel Dantas da Cruz, Greene explains why comparison should attend to differences as well as connections, and why an Atlantic frame may need wider hemispheric reach. He also acknowledges the danger that histories of negotiation among colonial elites can reproduce settlers’ self-justifications. His emphasis on colonial autonomy is therefore presented alongside an explicit warning about the costs of expansion to Indigenous peoples and enslaved Africans.
